name: Engineered Equipment Co-Alaska
old_description: The company specializes in the design and manufacturing of power generation systems and automatic transfer switches for low and medium voltage applications.
about:
Engineered Equipment Company was established in Anchorage, Alaska, in 1967 by Richard (Dick) W. Spils, an engineer with Standard Oil who recognized the need for a local representative to serve industrial product manufacturers in the state. The firm has maintained a continuous presence in Alaska since its inception. In 1994, J. Mark Wilson acquired the company and expanded its reach; a second office opened in Bothell, Washington, in 2016 to cover Washington, Oregon, and Idaho.

The company operates as a manufacturer's representative and distributor for leading brands of electrical equipment, valves, pumps, and process measurement and control instrumentation. With offices in Anchorage and Bothell, it serves industrial and heavy commercial markets across the Northwest, providing technical consulting and application support for complex projects.

Its customer base includes process plants and large-scale commercial installations in sectors such as power generation, water and wastewater treatment, oil and gas, food and beverage, chemical processing, pulp and paper, semiconductor manufacturing, life sciences, higher education, health care, transportation, and infrastructure.

Engineered Equipment emphasizes a consultative approach, positioning itself as a technical resource that helps clients solve challenging applications. The company cites its longevity as Alaska's longest-operating manufacturer's representative for process control and electrical equipment, combined with responsive service and demonstrated technical competence, as the foundation of its client relationships.
